bull_bear.body: Diversified revenue streams contribute to resilience
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- A dividend of 125%, i.e. Rs. 12.5 per equity share of Rs. 10 each, for 2025-26 was paid on 1 August 2026 - recommended by the Board and approved by shareholders at the AGM.
- Total debt stood at Rs. 482 Cr as at Jun-26 (Term Loan Rs. 248 Cr, Cash Credit/WCDL Rs. 234 Cr) versus Rs. 511 Cr at Jun-25 (216 / 295) and Rs. 691 Cr at Mar-26 (271 / 420).
- Stock position as on 30 June 2026 was Rs. 379 Cr (sugar stock Rs. 293 Cr, molasses / ethanol / other stocks Rs. 86 Cr) versus Rs. 456 Crores as on 30 June 2025.
- Shareholding as on 30 June 2026: promoters 61%, individual/HUF 30%, others including NRIs 9%; free float 39%, market cap Rs. 647 Cr, free-float market cap Rs. 252 Cr on 1.41 Cr shares outstanding.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated sugar-ethanol-power model across three Bihar facilities all within a 125 km radius, enabling shared logistics and fuller utilisation of every tonne of cane crushed.
- Deep, decade-plus relationships with approximately 88,500 farmers across three command areas, reinforced by prompt cane payment (within 14 days), supporting reliable cane supply and farmer loyalty in a region of intensifying competition for land and labour.
- Accounts for approximately 50% of Bihar's organised sugar sector.
- Stable, asset-light wholesale distribution network across five States, with all broker/sub-broker partners associated with the Company for over six years; long-term supply agreements with oil marketing companies (OMCs) underpin distillery revenue visibility.
- High institutional continuity: approximately 58% of the 1,152-strong workforce (as of 31 March 2026) has been with the Company since its 2015 incorporation, supporting operational discipline and process quality.
- Stable credit profile: CARE A+/Stable long-term and CARE A1 short-term bank facility ratings, reaffirmed/assigned during the year.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographical/logistics risk between mills and cane-growing areas — Operational efficiency may be affected by the distance between the Company's sugar mills and sugarcane cultivation areas, potentially causing logistical challenges and higher transportation costs; mitigated by locating mills within a 30-kilometre radius of key cane-growing regions with road connectivity.
- Cane procurement risk — Availability of high-quality sugarcane is critical to operations; any disruption in procurement or decline in cane quality could adversely affect production volumes and profitability. The Company relies on long-term relationships with approximately 88,500 cane farmers to secure stable supply.
- Cane quality risk — Procurement of substandard sugarcane may impact recovery rates, production efficiency and final product quality; the Company promotes early-maturing varieties and farmer awareness programmes to mitigate this.
- Financial/leverage risk — Rising debt levels could expose the Company to liquidity pressures and impact profitability and overall financial stability, in a business already carrying long-term debt and a sub-2x interest coverage/DSCR profile disclosed in the ratio table.
- Human capital risk — Inability to attract, retain and nurture skilled professionals may hinder operational efficiency, innovation and long-term growth.
- Policy and political uncertainty — Government decisions on export quotas, subsidies, ethanol blending and cane/sugar pricing policies directly impact industry profitability and stability; the Company operates in a heavily policy-influenced commodity business.
- Competition from unorganised sweeteners (gur/khandsari) — Traditional sweeteners such as gur and khandsari compete with refined sugar in rural and semi-urban markets, structurally capping refined sugar demand growth in parts of the Company's addressable market.
- Global sugar price volatility — Global sugar price fluctuations driven by climate events, trade barriers and production changes in major producers such as Brazil can impact Indian exports and domestic pricing, and therefore the Company's realisations.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Sugar and energy segments contribute to revenue
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Incorporated in 1932, with the group in the sugar business for over nine decades; the present company was formed in 2015 pursuant to a scheme of merger and demerger, manufacturing sugar, ethanol and power.
- Deck claims integrated operations across Sugar, Distillery and Co-Gen, patronage of the K.K. Birla Group (established in 1932 by Late Dr. Krishna Kumar Birla), excellent corporate governance, highly experienced management, healthy financials and sustainable EBITDA.
- Long-term credit rating upgraded to A+ by India Ratings and Research Pvt Ltd on 08 May 2026.
- Entirely Bihar-based footprint across Paschim Champaran, Gopalganj and Samastipur; the deck notes Bihar's sugar industry is shifting from simply operating existing mills towards revival, modernisation and integrated sugar-ethanol-power projects.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [FRP] The Government raised the Sugarcane FRP for SS 2026-27 by 2.81% to Rs. 365/qtl, up from Rs. 355/qtl.
- [Bihar policy] Bihar approved the Sugarcane Industry Investment Promotion Policy 2026 to attract fresh investment and modernise sugar mills, ethanol/distilleries and co-generation/power projects; revival of closed sugar mills remains a government priority. Bihar's SS 2025-26 sugar output is reported at around 5.8 LMT versus approximately 6.1 LMT the previous season.
- [Ethanol policy] Ethanol blending reached 20% as on 30 June 2026 (ESY 21-22: 10.02%, 22-23: 12.00%, 23-24: 14.60%, 24-25: 19.17%); NITI Aayog, with an inter-ministerial group, is working on a roadmap for blending targets beyond E20.
- [Industry balance - company estimates] SS 2025-26 estimated: opening stock 47 LMT, production 278 LMT, total availability 325 LMT, domestic consumption 270 LMT, exports 8 LMT, closing stock 47 LMT (about two months of domestic consumption); the Government has indicated any SS 2026-27 export decision will depend on production estimates after the monsoon assessment, likely around September 2026.
- [Key risks] Monsoon variability and possible El Nino impact, delay in export permissions, regulatory intervention if sugar prices rise sharply, revision in ethanol pricing, and increases in FRP or SAP without corresponding sugar price increases.
- [Transformative agenda] Five pillars - Digitalisation of Operations, Rising Capital Expenditure, Governance, Systems-oriented ('Magadh Way of Doing Things', reducing dependence on individual personalities) and People.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company operates three sugar mills in Bihar (Narkatiaganj, Sidhwalia, Hasanpur) with a combined licensed cane crushing capacity of 21,500 TCD, alongside integrated distilleries (155 KLPD, producing B-Heavy and C-Heavy route ethanol and industrial spirits) and co-generation power plants (38 MW) that utilise bagasse. It sells refined white crystal sugar through a wholesale broker/sub-broker network spanning five States, supplies ethanol under long-term agreements with oil marketing companies, and sells surplus power and by-products such as molasses and press mud.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Sugar:** White crystal sugar
- **Distillery:** Ethanol (B-Heavy route), Ethanol (C-Heavy route), Industrial spirits
- **Power:** Bagasse-based surplus (co-generation) power
- **By-products:** Molasses, Press mud

outlook.body: Outlook: Stable; Strategy: Focus on sustainable energy and sugar production
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body:
- Deepen integration across sugar, ethanol and power operations to improve resource utilisation and generate higher value from every tonne of cane crushed.
- Transition distilleries to multi-feed (grain plus molasses) capability to extend operating days, reduce dependence on seasonal molasses availability, and respond more dynamically to ethanol demand/pricing.
- Intensify cane varietal diversification and replacement (away from the red-rot-affected Co 0238 variety) through farmer engagement, agronomic guidance and cane development programmes.
- Maintain cost optimisation, liquidity management and working-capital efficiency, with specific emphasis on reducing cane outstandings owed to farmers to reinforce grower relationships.
- Build a more diversified, less cyclical and cash-efficient business model by reducing dependence on cyclical sugar revenues, backed by capacity enhancement, distillery integration and varietal transition.
- Maintain a disciplined capex freeze pending policy clarity as part of preserving shareholder wealth and balance-sheet resilience.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company expanded crushing capacity at its Narkatiaganj unit from 7,500 TCD to 10,000 TCD and, during the year, made the plant fully efficient under the C boiling scheme through debottlenecking; with this and steam-saving measures complete, it is now installing a sugar refinery at Narkatiaganj to add value and strengthen realisation. Both the Narkatiaganj and Sidhwalia distilleries (combined 155 KLPD) have been converted to multi-feed configurations - able to process molasses, cane syrup and grain - extending annual operating days beyond the ~270-day conventional molasses-only season and decoupling distillery operation from the length of the crushing season. At Hasanpur, a grain-based distillery is being evaluated for future development, given its location adjacent to the 'maize bowl' of Bihar; this remains at an evaluation stage, not a committed project.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's ethanol blending programme is viewed as one of the most significant structural growth drivers for the domestic sugar industry, and integrated players with multi-feed flexibility are seen as well positioned to benefit.
- Near-term outlook is closely linked to the 2026 Southwest Monsoon; IMD forecasts of below-normal rainfall and possible El Nino development raise concerns over cane availability, sugar recovery and production costs.
- Policy support - including a possible revision in the Minimum Selling Price (MSP) and the Government's decision to restrict sugar exports until September 2026 to safeguard domestic availability - is flagged as important for industry stability.
- Higher crushing throughput at Narkatiaganj enhances internal molasses generation, reducing dependence on externally procured molasses (which carries elevated logistics/procurement cost) and improving sugar-distillery integration economics.
- Ethanol supply to oil marketing companies carries shorter receivable cycles than sugar, so growing the distillery mix is expected to improve cash conversion and reduce reliance on short-term borrowings.
- Management expects progressive strengthening in revenues, margins and cash flows as varietal changes stabilise and distillery operational efficiencies improve.
- Elevated statutory cane price increases (cane cost per quintal raised during the year) and range-bound sugar realisations compressed margins across the sector during the year, reinforcing the importance of scale, efficiency and diversification.
- Long-term supply agreements with oil marketing companies (OMCs) underpin revenue visibility for the distillery/ethanol segment.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Magadh Sugar & Energy Limited has been upgraded to 'IND A+' with a Stable Outlook by India Ratings and Research, reflecting its improved credit profile and stable business operations. The company's diversified revenue streams from sugar and energy segments contribute to its resilience. However, the industry's volatility and regulatory risks may impact its performance.

open.item: Expand Narkatiaganj sugar unit crushing capacity from 7,500 TCD to 10,000 TCD, going on steam by November-December 2024.
Narkatiaganj expansion carries total invested capital cost of ~Rs 141 crores and is expected to deliver EBITDA of not less than 25%.
Narkatiaganj steam-saving measures to reduce steam consumption from ~44.7% to 34.8%.
Convert Sidhwalia molasses-based distillery to a multi-feed (grain/maize/rice) distillery at a capital cost of ~Rs 32 crores.
Company plans to complete all announced capex projects (Narkatiaganj expansion and Sidhwalia multi-feed conversion) during the current financial year FY25.
With the Narkatiaganj capacity increase, crushing at that unit is expected to rise by 28% to 29%.
Execute varietal replacement plan to replace red-rot-infested CO 238 cane with CO0118 and CO9301, keeping any single variety between 30% and 40% next season to improve recovery.
Management intends to reduce debt to gain financial flexibility and lower finance costs, freeing capital for value-creating projects.
Post multi-feed conversion, Sidhwalia distillery (150 KLPD) can run up to 340 days and produce up to ~5.50 crore litres of ethanol annually.
Company sees scope to grow cane crushed from ~237 lakh quintals last season up to ~288 lakh quintals as saturation point not yet reached.
If government grants full freedom, company intends to shift product mix back toward roughly 90% B-heavy/juice and 10% C-heavy, subject to price economics.
Maize availability of ~1 lakh MT from Samastipur, Begusarai and Khagaria against a daily requirement of ~260 MT/day secures feedstock for the multi-feed distillery.
New ethanol policy restricting C-molasses usage limits distillery utilisation (not more than ~3.8-3.9 cr litres vs 5.5 cr potential), the key rationale for multi-feed conversion.
Bihar low-land flooding and red-rot infestation of CO 238 variety are flagged risks to cane recovery, mitigated via embankments and topography-based variety selection.

wtt.summary: Building track record — 1Q logged, no reconciled verdicts yet.
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and forward-leaning on capex delivery within FY25; management candidly owned the lower cane recovery (red-rot in CO 238) and flagged ethanol-policy and flooding constraints rather than glossing over them.

Availability of high-quality sugarcane is critical to operations; any disruption in procurement or decline in cane quality could adversely affect production volumes and profitability. The Company relies on long-term relationships with approximately 88,500 cane farmers to secure stable supply.

Procurement of substandard sugarcane may impact recovery rates, production efficiency and final product quality; the Company promotes early-maturing varieties and farmer awareness programmes to mitigate this.

Rising debt levels could expose the Company to liquidity pressures and impact profitability and overall financial stability, in a business already carrying long-term debt and a sub-2x interest coverage/DSCR profile disclosed in the ratio table.
Inability to attract, retain and nurture skilled professionals may hinder operational efficiency, innovation and long-term growth.

Government decisions on export quotas, subsidies, ethanol blending and cane/sugar pricing policies directly impact industry profitability and stability; the Company operates in a heavily policy-influenced commodity business.

Traditional sweeteners such as gur and khandsari compete with refined sugar in rural and semi-urban markets, structurally capping refined sugar demand growth in parts of the Company's addressable market.

Global sugar price fluctuations driven by climate events, trade barriers and production changes in major producers such as Brazil can impact Indian exports and domestic pricing, and therefore the Company's realisations.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Magadh Sugar & Energy Limited is an integrated Bihar-based sugar, ethanol/distillery and co-generation power producer, part of the K.K. Birla Group, positioned as a strong proxy for the region's organised sugar industry.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company operates three sugar mills in Bihar (Narkatiaganj, Sidhwalia, Hasanpur) with a combined licensed cane crushing capacity of 21,500 TCD, alongside integrated distilleries (155 KLPD, producing B-Heavy and C-Heavy route ethanol and industrial spirits) and co-generation power plants (38 MW) that utilise bagasse. It sells refined white crystal sugar through a wholesale broker/sub-broker network spanning five States, supplies ethanol under long-term agreements with oil marketing companies, and sells surplus power and by-products such as molasses and press mud.

group_structure.body: - Mrs. Nandini Nopany — related party: Mother of Mr. Chandra Shekhar Nopany (Promoter Chairperson); disclosed as relative of key management personnel under Ind-AS 24 related-party disclosures.

guidance.title: Guidance / outlook
guidance.body: Outlook: Stable; Strategy: Focus on sustainable energy and sugar production

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's ethanol blending programme is viewed as one of the most significant structural growth drivers for the domestic sugar industry, and integrated players with multi-feed flexibility are seen as well positioned to benefit.
- Near-term outlook is closely linked to the 2026 Southwest Monsoon; IMD forecasts of below-normal rainfall and possible El Nino development raise concerns over cane availability, sugar recovery and production costs.
- Policy support - including a possible revision in the Minimum Selling Price (MSP) and the Government's decision to restrict sugar exports until September 2026 to safeguard domestic availability - is flagged as important for industry stability.
- Higher crushing throughput at Narkatiaganj enhances internal molasses generation, reducing dependence on externally procured molasses (which carries elevated logistics/procurement cost) and improving sugar-distillery integration economics.
- Ethanol supply to oil marketing companies carries shorter receivable cycles than sugar, so growing the distillery mix is expected to improve cash conversion and reduce reliance on short-term borrowings.
- Management expects progressive strengthening in revenues, margins and cash flows as varietal changes stabilise and distillery operational efficiencies improve.
- Elevated statutory cane price increases (cane cost per quintal raised during the year) and range-bound sugar realisations compressed margins across the sector during the year, reinforcing the importance of scale, efficiency and diversification.
- Long-term supply agreements with oil marketing companies (OMCs) underpin revenue visibility for the distillery/ethanol segment.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company expanded crushing capacity at its Narkatiaganj unit from 7,500 TCD to 10,000 TCD and, during the year, made the plant fully efficient under the C boiling scheme through debottlenecking; with this and steam-saving measures complete, it is now installing a sugar refinery at Narkatiaganj to add value and strengthen realisation. Both the Narkatiaganj and Sidhwalia distilleries (combined 155 KLPD) have been converted to multi-feed configurations - able to process molasses, cane syrup and grain - extending annual operating days beyond the ~270-day conventional molasses-only season and decoupling distillery operation from the length of the crushing season. At Hasanpur, a grain-based distillery is being evaluated for future development, given its location adjacent to the 'maize bowl' of Bihar; this remains at an evaluation stage, not a committed project.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated sugar-ethanol-power model across three Bihar facilities all within a 125 km radius, enabling shared logistics and fuller utilisation of every tonne of cane crushed.
- Deep, decade-plus relationships with approximately 88,500 farmers across three command areas, reinforced by prompt cane payment (within 14 days), supporting reliable cane supply and farmer loyalty in a region of intensifying competition for land and labour.
- Accounts for approximately 50% of Bihar's organised sugar sector.
- Stable, asset-light wholesale distribution network across five States, with all broker/sub-broker partners associated with the Company for over six years; long-term supply agreements with oil marketing companies (OMCs) underpin distillery revenue visibility.
- High institutional continuity: approximately 58% of the 1,152-strong workforce (as of 31 March 2026) has been with the Company since its 2015 incorporation, supporting operational discipline and process quality.
- Stable credit profile: CARE A+/Stable long-term and CARE A1 short-term bank facility ratings, reaffirmed/assigned during the year.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Diversified revenue streams contribute to resilience

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen integration across sugar, ethanol and power operations to improve resource utilisation and generate higher value from every tonne of cane crushed.
- Transition distilleries to multi-feed (grain plus molasses) capability to extend operating days, reduce dependence on seasonal molasses availability, and respond more dynamically to ethanol demand/pricing.
- Intensify cane varietal diversification and replacement (away from the red-rot-affected Co 0238 variety) through farmer engagement, agronomic guidance and cane development programmes.
- Maintain cost optimisation, liquidity management and …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [FRP] The Government raised the Sugarcane FRP for SS 2026-27 by 2.81% to Rs. 365/qtl, up from Rs. 355/qtl.
- [Bihar policy] Bihar approved the Sugarcane Industry Investment Promotion Policy 2026 to attract fresh investment and modernise sugar mills, ethanol/distilleries and co-generation/power projects; revival of closed sugar mills remains a government priority. Bihar's SS 2025-26 sugar output is reported at around 5.8 LMT versus approximately 6.1 LMT the previous season.
- [Ethanol policy] Ethanol blending reached 20% as on 30 June 2026 (ESY 21-22: 10.02%, 22-23: 12.00%, 23-24: 14.60%, 24-25: 19.17%); NITI Aayog, with an inter-ministerial group, is working on a roadmap for blending targets beyond E20.
- [Industry balance - company estimates] SS 2025-26 estimated: opening stock 47 LMT, production 278 LMT, total availability 325 LMT, domestic consumption 270 LMT, exports 8 LMT, closing stock 47 LMT (about two months of domestic consumption); the Government has indicated any SS 2026-27 export decision will depend on production estimates after the monsoon assessment, likely around September 2026.
- [Key risks] Monsoon variability and possible El Nino impact, delay in export permissions, regulatory intervention if sugar prices rise sharply, revision in ethanol pricing, and increases in FRP or SAP without corresponding sugar price increases.
- [Transformative agenda] Five pillars - Digitalisation of Operations, Rising Capital Expenditure, Governance, Systems-oriented ('Magadh Way of Doing Things', reducing dependence on individual personalities) and People.

themes.title: Bioenergy / Ethanol / SAF transition
themes.need: Higher ethanol-blending mandates (E20->E25/E27/E30), CBG, SAF and bio-IBA underpin a multi-year bioenergy capex cycle. PRAJIND's near-term earnings are depressed by a 1G slowdown + GenX gestation but the optionality (SAF, CBG, DC-cooling) is large; TRUALT/BALRAMCHIN/EIDPARRY/TRIVENI/GODAVARIB add ethanol/sugar; BCLIND/GULPOLY/GLOBUSSPR on grain-based distillation.
themes.driver: Higher blending-mandate notifications; SAF/CBG order conversion; sugar-cycle realisations.
